symptom: A FLOAT32 embedding stored as hash bytes was returned through a search projection in a representation that could not be reconstructed as the original NumPy array.
After several thousand 120-dimensional vectors were indexed, some vectors known to exist stopped appearing in HNSW FT.SEARCH results.
Background HSET updates against a roughly 100-million-row HNSW workload coincided with FT.SEARCH latency spikes from milliseconds to about one second.
A TEXT field indexed from an array of JSON objects did not consistently return the expected document for a value visibly present at the configured JSONPath.
Adding an unindexed JSONPath to FT.SEARCH RETURN caused HIGHLIGHT to fail although the indexed text fields and search term were otherwise valid.
FT.CREATE rejected a JSON TAG schema when SORTABLE preceded INDEXEMPTY and INDEXMISSING, while accepting the same options in another order.
TS.RANGE aggregation produced a valid aggregate whose bucket timestamp preceded the requested start, creating confusion about alignment and bucket boundaries.
After importing an RDB and rebalancing an authenticated cluster, TIMESERIES.REFRESHCLUSTER repeatedly reported an uninitialized cluster and inconsistent query behavior.
Time-series label names containing punctuation could be stored but filters using those label names silently returned no matches.
TS.RANGE with reversed bounds plus TWA aggregation and EMPTY terminated the server connection, whereas related range combinations returned an empty result.
